chapter.title: Standing up

cards.body:
The first swimming skill has nothing to do with going anywhere. It's standing up.

Think of the water as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through. You already get out of bed every morning, and in the pool the move has the same shape: **knees in, hands press down, feet on the floor**.
cards.simpler: The first thing to learn in swimming isn't moving forward. It's standing up. Think of the water as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through. You get out of bed every morning, and in the pool the move has the same shape: **knees in, hands press down, feet on the floor**.

cards.prompt: You're stretched out face-forward in chest-deep water, holding nothing, chin on the surface like a crocodile. You want to stand. What moves first?

options.text: Your hands, reaching down to touch the pool floor
Your knees, curling up toward your chest
Your legs, kept straight and swung down like a gate

whyNot.a: That's reaching for a floor, not pressing on a bed: your hands push the water down, they don't go looking for tiles.
whyNot.c: That's a gate, not a tuck: long straight legs swing slowly and tip you, while bent knees bring your feet under you fast.

cards.reteach: Think of getting out of bed in the dark: you curl up before you put your feet down. In water, pulling your knees toward your chest is what lets your feet swing under your hips. Once they're under you, standing is easy.

cards.title: Knees, hands, feet
cards.body:
**Knees in, hands press, feet down.** That's the whole move, in that order. From lying forward, lift your chin a little and pull your knees toward your chest, like curling up under a duvet. Your feet swing under your hips on their own.

At the same time, press both palms down and back toward your thighs, the way you'd push on the cushions to get up from a low sofa. Pushing the water down lifts your shoulders up.

Then plant your feet flat, a little apart. It takes under 2 seconds. Slow is fine. The water waits.
cards.simpler: **Knees in, hands press, feet down.** Do it in that order. Lying face forward, lift your chin a little and pull your knees to your chest. Your feet will swing under your hips by themselves. At the same time, press both palms down and back toward your thighs, like pushing up from a low sofa. Pushing water down lifts your shoulders up. Then put your feet flat, a little apart. It takes under 2 seconds. Going slow is fine.

cards.title: Dev's ten tries
cards.body: Dev, 34, is in the shallow end on a Tuesday evening, water at his chest. He holds the rail, stretches out with his chin on the water, lets go, and counts: knees, hands, feet. His first try is a frantic second and a mouthful of chlorine, because he forgot the hands. On the second he presses down hard, like closing an overstuffed suitcase, and he's standing before he's finished thinking about it. By the tenth he's bored, which is exactly the goal.
cards.simpler: Dev, 34, stands in the shallow end on a Tuesday evening, water up to his chest. He holds the rail, lies forward with his chin on the water, lets go, and counts: knees, hands, feet. His first try is a panicky second and a mouthful of chlorine, because he forgot his hands. On the second he **presses down hard**, like shutting a stuffed suitcase, and he's up before he knows it. By the tenth he's bored. That's the goal.

cards.prompt: Mia is lying forward, chin on the water, when a wave from the next lane slaps her face. She wants her feet down right now. Which move gets her there fastest?

options.text: Legs straight down, arms reaching up toward the pool edge
Knees pulled in, palms pressing down toward her thighs, feet planted
A big kick to reach the wall first, then stand

whyNot.a: That's reaching up, not pressing down: arms going up push your body down, and straight legs swing slowly.
whyNot.c: That's running from the problem, not solving it: the floor is right under her, closer than any wall.

cards.reteach: The floor is always closer than the wall. Pull your knees in so your feet swing under you, and press your hands down so your shoulders rise. Push the water down and you come up.

cards.body: Jo slips while standing up, and her arms shoot toward the sky as if to grab a rope that isn't there. Every arm that leaves the water pushes her body down, so she sinks lower and reaches higher. The tell: **if your hands are above the water, you're climbing a ladder that doesn't exist.** Put them back in and press down.
cards.simpler: Jo slips while standing up and throws her arms toward the sky, as if grabbing a rope that isn't there. But every arm that leaves the water pushes her body down. So she sinks lower and reaches higher. Here's the sign to watch for: **if your hands are above the water, you're climbing a ladder that doesn't exist.** Put them back in and press down.

cards.prompt: Why does pressing your palms down toward your thighs help you stand up?

options.text: It's like waving to the lifeguard, so someone sees you
It makes you sink faster, so your feet touch the floor sooner
It pushes water down, which lifts your shoulders while your knees bring your feet under you

whyNot.a: That's signalling, not standing: waving lifts your arms out of the water, which pushes you down.
whyNot.b: That's the straight-leg drop, not the press: your feet get under you because your knees pull in, while your hands lift your top half.

cards.reteach: Water pushes back on whatever pushes it. Press it down and it lifts your chest and shoulders, which gives your knees time to swing your feet underneath. That's why hands go down, never up.

cards.body: Tonight, on your actual bed: lie face down, arms stretched ahead. Count knees, hands, feet: pull your knees under you, press your palms into the mattress, and come up to kneeling. Five times. Your body learns the order dry.
cards.simpler: Tonight, try it on your own bed. Lie face down with your arms stretched out ahead. Count knees, hands, feet: pull your knees under you, press your palms into the mattress, and come up to kneeling. Do it five times. **Your body learns the order** while you're still dry.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
In water, **curl up and push the water down**: knees in, hands pressing, feet planted. From lying forward, that's knees in, hands press, feet down, and you're standing in under 2 seconds.

Tomorrow: your face goes in, and the trick is breathing out, not holding.
cards.simpler: In water, **curl up and push the water down**. Pull your knees in, press with your hands, and put your feet flat. From lying face forward, it's knees in, hands press, feet down, and you're standing in under 2 seconds. Tomorrow your face goes in the water, and the trick there is to breathe out, not hold your breath.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now go from lying forward in chest-deep water to standing in under 2 seconds.

repairedFrom.why: 'Low is steady' brings in two new skills, getting in by the steps and walking, that no exercise tests, so the chapter teaches more than one thing and loses focus.
repairedFrom.fix: Move the getting-in and walking material to its own chapter, retitle this one 'Standing up', and end on the 'Tomorrow: your face goes in…' line instead of the try card.
